summary: SYN-cookie enabled customer firewall causes gRPC connection flaps and HTTP/2 stream resets for streaming responses
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported intermittent streaming failures and fast client disconnects from Redwood Private agents. Impact: Live streaming endpoints (chat/streaming generate) experience repeated HTTP/2 RST_STREAM and full gRPC connection resets leading to truncated responses for ~10% of requests during peak. Symptoms started after a firewall rule update on customer's edge NGFW that enabled SYN cookie protection.

Context: Customer runs Redwood Private in a VPC peered to their on-prem via an edge NGFW. Traffic to the Redwood control plane and model-serving endpoints traverses the customer's firewall (stateful inspection) which recently had a policy change to harden TCP handshake handling (SYN cookie enabled).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From a client in the customer's network, open a streaming generation request to Redwood Private with HTTP/2 gRPC (long-lived).
2) Simulate connection churn by opening 20 concurrent streams and closing/reopening several to exercise connection reuse.
3) Observe periodic RST_STREAM errors and gRPC UNAVAILABLE followed by successful reconnects.
4) Disable SYN cookie feature on the firewall and repeat - streaming failures stop within 10 minutes.
logs_and_traces:
- Agent logs: repeated 'HTTP/2 stream reset (RST_STREAM code 2)' and 'gRPC transport error: connection closed' around timestamps 2026-03-10T15:22:41Z - 15:40:12Z.
- tcpdump (customer capture): server-side SYN seen, SYN-ACK returned, then server retransmits SYN-ACK and client sends ACK twice leading to ambiguous handshake. Observed duplicate SYN/ACK retransmits around 1-2s after initial handshake.
- Firewall logs: entries showing 'SYN-cookie engaged' and 'TCP handshake revalidated' for connections toward Redwood control plane IP range.
- Console metrics: increased CONNECT_FAILURE and short-lived streams metric for customer in us-east-1 between 15:20-16:00 UTC.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: firewall SYN cookie mechanism rewrites or suppresses early SYN/ACK leading to server-side view of handshake state mismatch and spurious retransmissions; gRPC connection reuse and HTTP/2 multiplexing amplify the effect into stream resets.
Reproduced in lab by enabling SYN cookie emulation on a test NGFW - identical RST_STREAM patterns observed.
Root cause confirmed by vendor packet-inspection analysis: the NGFW treats certain SYN retransmissions as malformed and injects SYN-cookie responses, but does not consistently forward the subsequent ACK to the original server instance when pooling connections across HA pair, resulting in half-open or duplicate-seen handshakes.
Correlated with recent firewall policy rollout at the customer's edge on 2026-03-09 23:00 UTC.
comments: Support (Maya): Logged by customer support after initial report; collected pcap and console metrics and escalated to SRE.

SRE (Sanjay): Confirmed patterns in packet capture; reproduced with vendor lab configuration. Opened ticket with customer's NGFW vendor: case #VENDOR-8821 and linked Slack thread #support-private-networking.

Customer (Ops lead, Aaron Li): Applied temporary rule tweak to disable SYN cookie on 2026-03-11 03:10 UTC; observed immediate reduction in stream resets. Customer requested a recommended long-term firewall config to maintain hardening without impacting gRPC streams.

SRE (Sanjay): Proposed mitigations: (1) disable SYN cookie for Redwood control-plane/model-serving IP ranges, (2) enable TCP connection tracking affinity on firewall HA pairs, (3) apply TCP keepalive and reduced idle timeouts on agents as defensive measure. Added runbook link: https://confluence.redwood.com/runbooks/private-networking-syn-cookie-workaround.
resolution:
Root cause: customer NGFW's SYN-cookie implementation was interfering with TCP handshake tracking across HA nodes, causing spurious retransmits and gRPC connection flaps.
Fix/Workaround applied: Customer disabled SYN-cookie for the Redwood destination CIDR and enabled connection-affinity for the firewall cluster. We recommended keeping TCP keepalive on the agent side and added a defensive retry/backoff change in the serving-runtime (non-breaking) to reduce impact during transient handshake anomalies.
Follow-up: Vendor provided firmware patch addressing cross-node SYN-cookie behavior (VND-1.4.2). Customer scheduled staged rollout for 2026-03-20. SRE implemented a non-disruptive retry backoff change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/1487) to make streaming more resilient.
